import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Box, Stack } from "@mui/material";
import type { ChangeEvent } from "react";
import { Button, TextField } from "@/Components/inputs";

interface JsonEditorProps<T = unknown> {
	data: T;
	onSave: (value: T) => void;
	label?: string;
	helperText?: string;
}

export const JsonEditor = <T,>({ data, onSave, label, helperText }: JsonEditorProps<T>) => {
	const [editMode, setEditMode] = useState(false);
	const [draftJson, setDraftJson] = useState(() => JSON.stringify(data, null, 2));
	const [savedData, setSavedData] = useState<T>(data);
	const [error, setError] = useState<string | undefined>();

	useEffect(() => {
		setSavedData(data);
		if (!editMode) {
			setDraftJson(JSON.stringify(data, null, 2));
		}
	}, [data, editMode]);

	const handleEdit = () => {
		setEditMode(true);
		setError(undefined);
	};

	const handleCancel = () => {
		setDraftJson(JSON.stringify(savedData, null, 2));
		setEditMode(false);
		setError(undefined);
	};

	const handleSave = () => {
		try {
			const parsed = JSON.parse(draftJson) as T;
			setSavedData(parsed);
			onSave(parsed);
			setEditMode(false);
			setError(undefined);
		} catch (err) {
			setError("Invalid JSON. Please fix syntax errors before saving.");
		}
	};

	const handleChange = (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
		setDraftJson(event.target.value);
		setError(undefined);
	};

	return (
		<Box>
			<Stack direction="row" spacing={1} mb={2}>
				<Button variant="outlined" onClick={handleEdit} disabled={editMode}>
					Edit
				</Button>
				<Button variant="contained" onClick={handleSave} disabled={!editMode}>
					Save
				</Button>
				<Button variant="text" onClick={handleCancel} disabled={!editMode}>
					Cancel
				</Button>
			</Stack>

			<TextField
				label={label ?? "JSON data"}
				multiline
				minRows={10}
				value={draftJson}
				onChange={handleChange}
				disabled={!editMode}
				fullWidth
				helperText={error ?? helperText}
				error={Boolean(error)}
			/>
		</Box>
	);
};
</attachment>

<ConfigBox
  title="Escalation Rules"
  subtitle="Send escalation alerts via selected channels after the configured delay."
  rightContent={
    <Stack spacing={theme.spacing(LAYOUT.MD)}>
      <Controller
        name="escalationAfter"
        control={control}
        render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
          <TextField
            value={field.value ?? ""}
            onChange={(e) => {
              const value = e.target.value;
              field.onChange(value === "" ? 0 : Number(value));
            }}
            type="number"
            fieldLabel="Escalation after (minutes)"
            placeholder="Enter minutes"
            fullWidth
            error={!!fieldState.error}
            helperText={fieldState.error?.message ?? ""}
          />
        )}
      />
      <Controller
        name="escalationNotificationChannels"
        control={control}
        render={({ field }) => {
          const notificationOptions = (notifications ?? []).map((n) => ({
            ...n,
            name: n.notificationName,
          }));
          const selectedNotifications = notificationOptions.filter((n) =>
            (field.value ?? []).includes(n.id)
          );
          return (
            <Autocomplete
              multiple
              options={notificationOptions}
              value={selectedNotifications}
              getOptionLabel={(option) => option.name}
              onChange={(_: unknown, newValue) => {
                field.onChange(newValue.map((n) => n.id));
              }}
              isOptionEqualToValue={(option, value) => option.id === value.id}
              renderInput={(params) => (
                <TextField
                  {...params}
                  fieldLabel="Escalation notification channels"
                  placeholder="Select notification channels"
                  fullWidth
                />
              )}
            />
          );
        }}
      />
    </Stack>
  }
/>

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Checkmate is an open-source uptime and infrastructure monitoring application. It monitors server hardware, uptime, response times, and incidents with real-time alerts. The companion agent [Capture](https://github.com/bluewave-labs/capture) provides infrastructure metrics (CPU, RAM, disk, temperature).

## Development Commands

### Client (React/Vite)
```bash
cd client
npm install
npm run dev              # Start dev server at http://localhost:5173
npm run build            # TypeScript check + production build
npm run lint             # ESLint (strict, max-warnings 0)
npm run format           # Prettier formatting
npm run format-check     # Check formatting
```

### Server (Node.js/Express)
```bash
cd server
npm install
npm run dev              # Start with hot-reload (nodemon + tsx) at http://localhost:52345
npm run build            # TypeScript compile + path alias resolution
npm run test             # Run Mocha tests with c8 coverage
npm run lint             # ESLint v9
npm run lint-fix         # Auto-fix lint issues
npm run format           # Prettier formatting
```

### Docker Development
```bash
cd docker/dev
./build_images.sh
docker run -d -p 27017:27017 -v uptime_mongo_data:/data/db --name uptime_database_mongo mongo:6.0
```

## Environment Setup

### Server `.env` (minimum required)
```env
CLIENT_HOST="http://localhost:5173"
JWT_SECRET="my_secret_key_change_this"
DB_CONNECTION_STRING="mongodb://localhost:27017/uptime_db"
TOKEN_TTL="99d"
ORIGIN="localhost"
LOG_LEVEL="debug"
```

### Client `.env`
```env
VITE_APP_API_BASE_URL="http://localhost:52345/api/v1"
VITE_APP_LOG_LEVEL="debug"
```

## Architecture

### Monorepo Structure
- `/client` - React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + MUI frontend
- `/server` - Node.js 20+ + Express + TypeScript backend
- `/docker` - Multi-environment Docker configs (dev, staging, prod, arm, mono)

### Backend Layers
```
server/src/
├── controllers/     # Route handlers (authController, monitorController, etc.)
├── service/         # Business logic
│   ├── business/    # Core monitoring logic
│   ├── infrastructure/  # Server/system utilities
│   └── system/      # App-level settings
├── db/
│   ├── models/      # Mongoose schemas (Monitor, Check, Incident, User, etc.)
│   ├── migration/   # Database migrations (run on startup)
│   └── modules/     # Database-specific modules
├── middleware/v1/   # verifyJWT, rateLimiter, sanitization, responseHandler
├── routes/v1/       # API route definitions
├── validation/      # Joi input validation schemas
└── repositories/    # Data access layer
```

### Frontend Structure
```
client/src/
├── Components/      # Reusable UI components
├── Pages/           # Page components (Auth, Uptime, Infrastructure, Incidents, etc.)
├── Features/        # Redux slices (Auth, UI)
├── Hooks/           # Custom React hooks
├── Utils/           # Utilities (NetworkService.js is main API client)
├── Validation/      # Input validation
└── locales/         # i18n translations
```

### API
- Base URL: `/api/v1`
- Documentation: `http://localhost:52345/api-docs` (Swagger UI)
- OpenAPI spec: `/server/openapi.json`

### Key Technologies
- **State Management**: Redux Toolkit + Redux-Persist
- **Data Fetching**: SWR + Axios
- **Database**: MongoDB with Mongoose ODM
- **Queue/Cache**: Redis + BullMQ + Pulse (cron scheduling)
- **i18n**: i18next + react-i18next (translations via PoEditor)

## Code Conventions

### Internationalization
All user-facing strings must use the translation function:
```javascript
t('your.key')  // Never hardcode UI strings
```

### Branching
- Always branch from `develop` (not master)
- Use descriptive names: `feat/add-alerts`, `fix/login-error`
- PRs target `develop` branch

### Formatting
- **Client**: Prettier with `printWidth: 90`, tabs, double quotes
- **Server**: Prettier with `printWidth: 150`, tabs, double quotes
- Both use ESLint with strict settings

### Testing
Server tests use Mocha + Chai + Sinon:
```bash
npm test                    # Run all tests with coverage
npm test -- --grep "pattern"  # Run specific tests
```
Test files: `server/tests/**/*.test.js`

## Database Models

Key Mongoose models in `/server/src/db/models/`:
- **Monitor** - Monitoring configuration (website, infrastructure, port, etc.)
- **Check** - Individual monitoring check results
- **Incident** - Downtime incidents
- **User** - User accounts
- **Team** - Team/workspace management
- **StatusPage** - Public status pages
- **Notification** - Alert configuration (email, Discord, Slack, webhooks)
- **MaintenanceWindow** - Scheduled maintenance periods
- **AppSettings** - Global application settings

## The failure reason

The log is still a Gmail auth failure:

- `535 5.7.8 … BadCredentials`

That means Gmail is rejecting the SMTP password.

---

## Most likely issue

Your new app password is being entered with spaces.

Google shows app passwords as 4 groups of 4 characters for display, but the actual password should be used as a single 16-character string.

So if your app password is shown as:

- `vgot caun unmm rizt`

then the value you must save is:

- `vgotcaununmmrizt`

(no spaces)

---

## What to do

1. Update `systemEmailPassword` to the exact 16 characters with no spaces.
2. Make sure `systemEmailUser` / `systemEmailAddress` is the exact Gmail address used to generate that app password.
3. Restart the server.
4. Try the `Test` button again.

---

## If you want to verify the DB directly

Run this in MongoDB:

```js
db.appsettings.findOne({}, {
  systemEmailHost: 1,
  systemEmailPort: 1,
  systemEmailSecure: 1,
  systemEmailAddress: 1,
  systemEmailUser: 1,
  systemEmailPassword: 1
})
```

If it still fails after that, the next thing is:

- confirm the app password belongs to `agarge057@gmail.com`
- confirm you are not using your normal Google login password

But first: remove spaces from the app password and retry.

**Analyzing web service status**

It seems they've ended the web service, but the Uptime dashboard is still green. I wonder if the Render service is the one that ended while the app continues running from a different deployment or an old container. The user could be using a hosted copy, resulting in the app being separate from the Render service. It looks like there's no direct connection between the service status and the dashboard, which only reflects successful checks.

**Crafting a clear response**

The dashboard updates only when a scheduled check fails. If the monitor’s interval is set to 5 minutes or longer, it could remain green until the next check. The monitor may need several failures to mark the service down, especially if it still returns a status 200 on a maintenance page. Ending the Render service makes it unreachable once fully stopped, but if it returns a "retry later" page, the monitor sees it as up. For immediate updates, manually trigger a check or adjust the monitor settings.

response.value:
## Why your dashboard still shows green

Because the monitor only turns red after checks actually fail.

### Most likely reasons

- The service is still being probed successfully by the app
- The monitor interval may be long, so it hasn’t checked again yet
- Render may still be returning a valid response or a maintenance page
- The monitored URL may not be the same endpoint you stopped

---

## What this means

Stopping the Render web service does not instantly force the dashboard to show “down”.

The app needs:
1. a failed check
2. enough time for the next scheduled probe
3. the correct target URL

---

## What to do

- Check the monitor’s configured URL and make sure it matches the service endpoint
- Wait for the next check interval
- If your monitor uses a 5-minute interval, it may take up to 5 minutes to change
- If you want faster detection, reduce the monitor interval or failure threshold in the monitor settings

---

## Quick sanity check

If you want the dashboard to reflect the actual stop:
- open the monitored URL in a browser
- if it still loads, the service is not actually down
- if it returns an error, wait for the next check and the dashboard should update

If you want, I can also help you find the monitor interval and failure logic in the app.
